sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Paths and imports
sections.what: Imports the export, ingestion and model steps, and sets the paths to the sample file, output folder and build database.
sections.why: Keeps all the file locations in one place so the script always uses the committed sample.
sections.watch_out: The paths are fixed relative to this file, so moving it changes where outputs are written.

sections.name: _hash
sections.title: File fingerprint helper
sections.what: Calculates the SHA-256 fingerprint of a file and returns it as text.
sections.why: Lets the manifest record a fingerprint for each sample output.
sections.watch_out: The whole file is read into memory, so very large outputs use a lot of memory.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Build and export the sample set
sections.what: Ingests the sample, builds the SOLAR-A model, writes the model JSON, exports the offline HTML and audit zip, and writes a manifest with file sizes and fingerprints. It then prints how many artifacts were produced.
sections.why: Likely reason: the generated set must be consistent and checkable, so the manifest records exactly what was produced.
sections.watch_out: The project ID SOLAR-A is fixed, so changing the sample file's project breaks the script.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Command entry point
sections.what: Runs the main function when the file is run directly.
sections.why: Lets the developer regenerate samples from the command line.

summary: Regenerates the committed sample outputs for the solar sample project: a model file, an offline HTML export, an audit zip, and a manifest with file sizes and hashes.
purpose: Keeps the sample outputs in the repository current and provides a checkable record of what each file contains.
why: Likely reason: committed samples let reviewers see the output without running the whole app, and hashes let them confirm the files are unchanged.
how: It creates the output folders, ingests the sample schedule into a build database, builds the SOLAR-A model, and writes the model JSON. It then exports the offline HTML and the audit zip. Finally it writes a manifest listing each file's size and SHA-256 hash.
inputs: The sample file samples/sample-multi-project.csv and the built frontend in frontend/dist.
outputs: Model JSON, offline HTML, audit zip and a sample-output-manifest.json in samples/generated, plus a temporary build database.
risks: The HTML export needs the built frontend. A missing frontend/dist folder will break the export.
debug: If the script fails, check that frontend/dist exists and that the sample file contains the SOLAR-A project. Compare the manifest hashes with the files to see what changed.
